reason: E1 and E3 support that higher-melting elements (Mo, Nb, Ta) improve elevated-temperature strength, and E2 explicitly replaces Ti/Zr with W to raise melting point and strength, supporting the first two premises. However, the cited evidence does not quantify a ~20% improvement at 1600°C (E1 reports 367 MPa at 1400°C for a different composition) nor directly confirm edge-dislocation strengthening as the dominant mechanism, leaving the third and fourth premises only partially supported.
premises: Replacing lower-melting elements (Ti, Zr) with higher-melting elements (Mo, Nb, Ta, W) increases the alloy's average melting point
Higher melting point of constituent elements directly improves elevated-temperature yield strength
The strengthening mechanism is edge-dislocation-induced solid-solution strengthening in a stable BCC phase
A ~20% or greater increase in yield strength at ~1600°C is achievable by this substitution
